title: The front door gained its small surfaces
summary: The door now sorts gently by what a visitor came for — Curious, to the Sphere and tonight's sky; Gardening, to the Pattern Garden, with the farm record's edge stated plainly where it does not yet reach; With children, to the Spark first, on a grown-up's device. A promises panel prints only the lines that are true today, and a visitor who is not ready leaves by a light thread — the daily shares — with nothing asked of them. On the Observatory, one tap now makes a clean picture of your own day, or your year, as it truly stands, captioned with the day's true name and made on your own device; nothing is uploaded by the making of it.

title: The sky line learned to say when it has no place
summary: Aaron's screenshot caught the Sphere's sky line printing a sunrise and a sunset — 9:44 PM and 9:49 AM — on a device that kept no place at all: arithmetic with no location in it, printed as fact. The cause was small and exact: the line read the kept place through a conversion that turns an absent coordinate into zero, so the sky was quietly computed for 0°, 0° and the times came out wrong by half the world. The rule now stands at the source: a coordinate counts only when it is present, and when no place is kept the line prints only what needs no place — the season, the solstice turn, the Moon's phase and light, which are true everywhere — and says plainly that sunrise, sunset and the drawn sky need a place, and where to set one. No time is printed that was not computed from a real location. With a place kept, nothing changes: the times print for that place, computed on the device, as they always have.

title: Witness tended its page on the day of the Whole Road
summary: The Witness page carries November 24: the Spark's inhabitant programme completed before dawn with the Whole Road, the Spark walking its own recorded history on the Sphere itself; the app build finished at Spark. Living Day version 0.6.0, Gates A through F complete, the candidate in Aaron's hands; and the Sphere page's own app mode landed on Aaron's word naming the merge, the last piece of Gate D. The same note records the honest remainder: the app still carries an older copy of the Sphere until its next bundle sync — the fancy new one stands on the site — and a small rebuild carrying the fresh copy is prepared and waiting on his tap.

title: The Sphere page took up its own app mode
summary: Gate D's last piece, merged on Aaron's word: when the Sphere is opened inside the Spark. Living Day app, the page itself now carries the app framing. A small boot script marks the page before first paint, in app context only, and the page's own stylesheet and module hold the framing the app designed for it — the site bars absent rather than slimmed, the guide resting as a pull-up sheet, the stage filling the given screen. On the open web nothing changes: without the app mark the module is inert and the stylesheet's every rule stands behind it. Until now the app held this identical framing by injection over its bundled copy of the page; the page's own mode now stands on the site, and the app takes it up at its next bundle sync — until then the injection carries the same framing, so the instrument reads identically either way. The change is exactly one protected page, the Living Time Sphere, altered by three insertions — the boot script, one stylesheet link, one script tag — admitted through the protection test's own signature route, with no geometry, rendering, camera, motion, selection, label, or calendar file touched. With this landing, every piece of Gate D stands built: the Observatory stage, the Day World, the history marks, and the page's own app face.

title: The Spark walked the Whole Road
summary: At Guardian breadth — a full Pattern year kept — the Spark can now perform its own keeping on the Sphere itself: the Whole Road. The programme is composed only from the record's own facts, in the order the phone's derivation names: the birth day, where the seed's motif sounds; the hums, sounded at the days their tokens came home, in the order they came home; the feats, each performed at the day it was learned, a learned route walking the days it was taught; and the first day closed together, where the road ends in rest. A shorter road walks the year's turning points only. The road stands offered in the Spark's book at any time, and at the year's reading on the Day Out of Time — always at the keeper's asking, never by itself — and a performance writes nothing: the record stands exactly as it stood. Where the year's days are not standing on the face, the road says so plainly and names the step instead of pretending to travel; where a station has not yet come around, it waits at the last true station for the instrument's turning. Below Guardian there is no hollow version: the book says what the road asks — a full year kept. With this slice, the inhabitant Aaron directed stands complete as designed: the Spark living in the instrument's real geometry, its life derived from the record and nothing else. One piece remains held by design, awaiting Aaron's word — a body rendered inside the 3D scene itself, which needs the protected renderer's own hooks.

title: The Spark learned the turning of the year
summary: The Spark now answers the year it lives in. Standing on the Sphere, it knows the season from the calendar's own facts: the Moon it stands in, named with its essence and its quarter of the Pattern year; a Moon's last day, when it names the Moon that closes and the one that opens next, and in its first ranging of the day crosses to the new Moon's first day and regards it; a Moon's first day, with the day just closed standing behind it; and the Year Gate, where it may cross to the old year's last day and look back. On the Day Out of Time and the Deep Time Day there is no plate to stand on, and none is pretended — the Spark keeps the threshold with its keeper, and rests. Inside an opened day it answers the day's own character: a birth day regarded with a glow, a garden day above the plainer marks, each mark with its posture. The care the design named stands complete now, each kind in its true place: kindling and rest in the Spark's panel on the Sphere; tending — the dressing of the Spark in its own glow, the hour's halo, or the flame wrap's firelight, each choice standing in the record; carrying in Their Home, where a keepsake or token taken up for the day rides with the Spark's light until it is taken back and the carrying closed; and Quiet Company inside an opened day, where the keeper simply sits with the Spark a while — no task, no game — and the sitting itself is written once. Their Home has a temper now — spare, settled, or full, counted from what truly stands in it — and the Spark ranges as the home allows. The site's two trick lists are one derivation at last: the companion core's kind tricks and the Sphere book's ruled signatures are the same feats under two names, each face reading the other's teaching, so no keeper loses a trick either face taught. And the first time a fetch carries a keepsake or a token home, the thing's own record gains one line — carried to you, and the day — never written twice, and named when the keeper reads the thing again. This is the fifth slice of the inhabitant Aaron directed; the Whole Road — the Spark performing its own kept history on the Sphere itself — is designed and named, and comes in its own slice.

title: The Spark's home filled with the journey
summary: The Spark's home now answers its history. Their Home reads the same record the Sphere reads — nothing placed by hand, nothing invented: the road so far stands in plain words (the stage the record paints, the Moons kept, the lands walked, the routes shown and the ones become the Spark's own, the tricks learned, the days closed together, the hums learned), the path's stones are gilded where the record marks a day beyond the keeping itself — a day witnessed, a token's homecoming, a practice, a birth — and the story corner stands in the world itself now, one token for each episode watched through. The carrying tricks stand learned the way the design derives them: Fetch the Token with the Bearer stage itself, performed in Their Home — name a keepsake on the shelf or a token in the corner, and the Spark travels the home ground, takes it up, carries it to the gate, and presents it, naming it with its day and its story, then returns it to its place; Carry the Lantern at Bearer, when a Waymaker skill stands met in an episode watched through and a practice stands sealed — carried lit at the Spark's station inside an opened day while the keeper reads. And every episode watched through has taught the Spark its hum: the repertoire stands in the trick book, and a hum is performed on the Sphere at the day its token came home, the motif sounded in the Spark's own voice. Performances and fetches write nothing; the home of a thin record is honestly spare, and a rich record's home is full, because the record is. This is the fourth slice of the inhabitant Aaron directed; the Whole Road and the season's reactions are designed and named, and come in their own slices.

title: The Spark learned tricks, and can be taught
summary: The Spark's keeping now leaves lines in the record — the first writing the inhabitant has done, and it is fenced the way the design rules: a line may name a shared act, a closing, or a learning, and may never carry a score, a streak, a count of performances, or anything losable. In the Spark's own panel on the Sphere stands its book: the tricks it can do, each with the act that taught it, and the ones it has not learned yet, each with plain words saying what would teach them. The Basics are there from birth. The Bow comes from the first day the two of you close together — and inside the day's own room that rite now stands, the Spark reading the day from the record before you leave it. The kind's signature comes when the keeping spans three kinds and its paired act stands in the record; the Bearer signature, in the names Aaron ruled, when the paired act stands in a second Moon. Ask for a learned trick and the Spark performs it on the Sphere itself — hopping and drifting across the real day plates, bowing, glowing, sounding its note, laying small lights on the days it crosses. And a keeper can teach: travel a route across days with the Spark following, and the way is written down as one line naming its days; when the Spark walks it back in another Moon, the route becomes its own. Performances and readings still write nothing — only shared acts and the landing of a learning do. This is the third slice of the inhabitant Aaron directed; the carrying tricks, Their Home keeping the journey, and the Whole Road are designed and named, and come in their own slices.

title: The Spark learned its keeper's ways
summary: The Spark's idle hours are no longer the same for every keeper. What it does when you are still — where it drifts, how far it ranges, which days it goes to — now grows from the breadth of your own record with it: the play you have shared, the lands you have walked, the Moons you have kept, the days you have witnessed, the practice you have kept, the tokens that have come home, and your Genesis birth day. Left alone, it may range the ring, or go to a day your life has marked and regard it — a discovery, made of nothing but the record's own facts — or rest beside a day that holds a keepsake. A panel in the Spark's own place on the Sphere says, in plain words, what it has come to favour and the facts each favour stands on; where the record is still thin, it says the Spark is still learning your ways, and its idle hours keep the plain defaults. Two Sparks of a kind now differ because their keepers' records differ. Nothing here is scored, nothing is losable, and this slice writes nothing to the record — a discovery is a reading, and readings write nothing. This is the second slice of the inhabitant Aaron directed; teaching by demonstration, Their Home keeping the journey, and the Whole Road are designed and named, and come in their own slices.

title: The Spark took up residence in the Sphere
summary: The Spark no longer circles above the Sphere's face. It stands on the calendar itself now: on today's plate when the page opens, and when you pick a day — in any Moon — it travels the ring to that day and stands there, moving the way it has always moved, a drift with a hop in it. Open a day and it steps through the door with you and takes its place inside the day's own room; come back out and it returns to the day you picked. Left alone, it lives a little on its own — sitting, watching, resting, or drifting to a nearby day to look — leaning on what you and it have actually played together, and any touch of yours ends it at once. Its light answers your own hour, warm in the morning and deep at night. This is the first slice of the inhabitant Aaron directed: travel on the real geometry, entering the day, idle life, and the day's light. Teaching by demonstration, preferences grown from breadth, Their Home keeping the journey, and the Whole Road are designed and named, and come in their own slices.

title: The Spark's fence was made whole
summary: An audit of the one-mind Spark design against the live site found two faults, and both are closed. The Spark's conversation on the Sphere's route stood outside the children's gate that guards the talking door on every other route, so a young keeper's words could have travelled; the gate now stands on that route too, and in child mode the Spark answers from the record on the device and sends nothing. And what a Spark comes to believe was kept in one store shared by every Spark in a browser; each Spark now keeps its own store, keyed by its seed, and whatever the old shared store held is carried into the keeper's own Spark — moved, not copied — so nothing a Spark already holds is lost, and nothing is left for another Spark to claim.

title: The Genesis Oracle became a standing profile
summary: The Genesis Oracle now works the way Aaron set for the Living Genesis Profile: create your profile once — birth date, and birth time if you know it — and it saves in your own browser, so your Seal of Becoming, your birth Moon and Day, your Tone, and your original reading are simply there when you return, stamped with the Oracle version that produced them. One profile can be marked My Genesis, and the page opens on it. The Daily Mirror still meets today, but now from that standing signature, and it marks your two birthdays as the different days they are: the Pattern recurrence, when your birth Moon and Day come round again, and your civil birthday. Recalculating never overwrites: it arrives as a new entry, with the original kept inside it. And the Sphere knows your birth position now — your seal beside it below the stage, one tap to travel there, and the panel lit when your birth day is the day on show.

title: Every page learned to say what it is
summary: A site-wide sweep of descriptions and share cards, on Aaron's word after the search listing showed an older era's framing. Every one of the 194 pages now carries its own description, a working share image, its social cards, and its favicon, each drawn from what the page itself holds. The homepage's description — the one the search engines show — now names the site as it stands: the Living Sphere, the Spark, the Episode Library, the Pattern Garden, and the Genesis Oracle standing as the living feature it is. Three broken share images were repaired, and the retired headline framing was lifted from the front descriptions.

title: The series took its new name: Free the Spark
summary: Aaron renamed the companions' series — first sketched as Free the Noods and the Companions, out of his Free the Noods work — and cleared it to go up under its new name: Free the Spark. The name covers the whole line; the game itself stays parked until its day, and the series' planned entries stand as planned, nothing filmed or playable yet. His own page now names the project Free the Spark.

title: The map, the pages and the Sphere now read one story
summary: The Traveller's Road now stands whole in its three places, every one of them read from the one story spine. The Traveller's Map carries the whole road beside the Library: each episode told apart by name, land, Moon and token — never by number — with its kin on the road named and a door into the Episode Library at its own anchor. The episodes still being written stand on the map and on the pages they will belong to as planned, with nothing to play yet — the Living Circuit's five among them: on the T-7's own page, in the Remnant Lab beside the Workshop's chapter, at the Sound Observatory, on the map itself, and on the Sphere. And on the Sphere, the Moon on show now offers its own episodes — choose a day, and the story of its Moon stands beside the instrument with a door to its film — carried on the companion layer, on the site's one calendar, with the protected instrument untouched and no second calendar anywhere.

title: The Sphere's details, gathered and finished
summary: Three small findings from the visual sweep that waited their turn inside the protected files, finished together at Aaron's word. The season and gate tags at the Sphere's rim no longer slice off at the stage's edge: each frame, a tag whose marker nears the edge is drawn the smallest step inward that keeps its word whole, and it stands on its marker again the moment the marker leaves the rim. The centre plaque's third line no longer reads “Deep Mirror — Name” — Day 25's archetype is named Name, and the bare word read as a placeholder never filled in; the line now carries the day's own archetype text, “Recover identity and purpose.”, and so for every day of the 364. And the year card's “temporal membrane” is gone from the face: in plain words, each year's marker is the same day in that year. The calendar's math, the days' spread and swell, and the labels' pace did not move.

title: The Sphere's days learned to breathe
summary: Three repairs Aaron named from his phone, made inside the protected Sphere files he opened for exactly these fixes. The day numbers no longer stand stuck together: the faced Moon's twenty-eight plates spread wider at arm's length, back at their natural size, and none of them touches another in any pose. As you approach a day its number now swells steadily — small and quiet at range, growing with closeness, full as you enter the day — and settles back as you pull away, always under the law that no two plates may touch. And the wording no longer drifts behind the turning Sphere: the labels re-draw at the pace the camera actually moves, not twice a second. The calendar's own math did not move; what changed is how the face presents it.

title: The Episode Library opened its doors
summary: The story's films now stand together in one room. Every film of the Traveller's Road plays where it stands, told apart by name, land, Moon and token — never by number — with its written chapter as its reading companion, and the vision trailer, finished and approved, opens the room as its feature presentation. A keeper's place is kept on their own device by the same watch record the story's pages keep: only a true watch counts, and a finished watch brings the token home, here as anywhere. The episodes still being written stand on their own shelf, named plainly as planned or scripted, with nothing to play yet — among them the Night Road's six, scripted in full, and the five of the Living Circuit, the series of the author's own device works, now registered in the story bible.

title: The Sphere took its keeper's corrections
summary: From the keeper's own phone, four corrections. The Evolution Opening's first-visit flag now belongs to the film itself: a visitor who met only the earlier staged walk still meets the film, and the flag is earned by the first painted frame — a load that never paints leaves no mark. The film's composed score is gone; in its place one deep cinematic swell at the root, swelling as the film opens and settling as the scrim lifts, silent until the first touch, as the sound rule has always held. The caption above the Sphere wraps whole again — no sentence cut mid-word at the stage's edge. And the Spark starts on its circuit from the first frame, never resting in the corner; when the Sphere is held still, it stations itself at its resting place instead of stopping wherever it was.

title: Witness tended its page on the day of designs
summary: The Witness page carries November 23: a charter drawn for the Sphere, a real sky computed on the device standing in review, a Front Door designed for new arrivals, the Sparks' page designed as a walkable 3D world, play redesigned simpler — and a new standard in Aaron's words, that the whole site should feel a little alive. The same change writes the growth record's missing entry for yesterday's tending and records Aaron's standing rule: every landing updates this log in the same change.

title: The garden learned to wait, and the games became quests
summary: The Pattern Garden is completed in the play redesign's simplified form. At a Moon's turn a planting is now graded kindly — slept, tended, kept, flourished — and a tended planting is never wasted: its seed is gathered back to head the same bed's table next year. Harvests earned in past years and keepsake returns that came due while their Moon was not open now wait at the garden's head until the keeper's hand gathers or welcomes them; nothing earned evaporates, and nothing is collected in the keeper's absence. The open bed's table stands whole, grouped by method, its plant buttons speak the days of the Moon that remain, and one planting per bed stands as law — a planting once written is never uprooted. On the Sphere, the three Observatory games now wear the quest frame, rung 1: once a day the Spark offers a question answerable only by reading the instrument, takes a one-tap prediction, and lets the game itself be the hunt; the reveal is stated as a count and an answer card is kept in the Life Atlas — a missed guess kept beside a true one, because the card records the learning, never a score. Catch the turning's minute stands as an attention frame only, and says so on its face: a turning not caught is not recorded. And the Still Bed now stands at the garden's foot — a fourteenth place, unnumbered, open only on the Day Out of Time and the Deep Time Day — where one keepsake of the year now ending may be laid in the still ground by its own record, never by editing the keepsake's, to be found at the next still day when the garden's head reads the year whole: thirteen beds, one line each — kept, flourished, tended, slept, rested.

title: The Sphere shows how it grew
summary: The first time a visitor comes to the Sphere now, it tells its own story in four short stages, standing over the living instrument: the 13 Moons lying flat as a calendar, with today marked; the first Sphere of July 2026, drawn again from that first build's own drawing code, its markers standing where the record places them today; the Sphere as it stands now, revealed live underneath; and the Spark, arriving to give the intro — turning, diving, the rings, and the keeping of a day. It is labelled a demonstration on its face, it can be skipped at every stage, it never stands in front of a shared view, and afterwards it waits quietly in the guide bar under the words See how it grew, for anyone who wants to walk it again.

title: The Codex of Reality and the Living Sphere — a white paper
summary: The whole work set down in one paper: the framework and its method, the 13 Moons, the Living Sphere and its layers, the Spark, and the Living Phone — as designed and as built, with the state of each part stated honestly and the author's open questions printed unresolved.

title: The Moons took their settled names
summary: The thirteen Moons now answer to one settled set of names everywhere the site speaks them — the Pattern Calendar's own set, Deep Mirror and Return Path among them — the same names on the Sphere's face, in the calendar, and in this record, held there by a test that pins them so the two sets cannot drift apart again.

title: The tracker left the site
summary: The site no longer keeps any count of its visitors. Google Analytics was removed from every page — all seventy-two of them, the Sphere's own page among them, opened for this one change — and a guard in the test suite now holds the count at zero, so it cannot creep back unnoticed.

title: The Spark learned to speak up, sparingly
summary: The Spark now offers small tips when the keeper's own record earns them — a harvest standing ready in the Pattern Garden, a keepsake that can return to its bed, a practice left unfinished — each one naming the record it came from, and none at all when the record is silent. A soft two-note chime, tuned to A=432, sounds first when the keeper allows sound; the keeper chooses chime, words only, spoken aloud, or quiet always, and any kind of tip can be dismissed forever. The fence screen runs before a tip is composed, so fenced ground never becomes a tip, and nothing is fetched from anywhere: every tip is composed on the keeper's own device, from their own record.

title: The sky came onto the Sphere
summary: The Sphere now works out its own sky on your device, with nothing fetched: sunrise, sunset and solar noon for the place you keep, the Moon’s phase and its rising and setting, the planets, the season turns for any year, and — at the night standing of the new sky dome — 510 real stars from the Yale Bright Star Catalogue, each placed by the math for where you stand and when. No place kept means no sky drawn, only the one honest sentence, as ever.

title: The river and the blossoms came onto the Sphere
summary: The Sphere's first test layers after the sky, both off until a keeper turns them on: the salmon counted past Bonneville Dam on the Columbia River, day by day from 1939 to 2026, counted by the Army Corps of Engineers and carried by Columbia River DART; and Kyoto's cherry-blossom full flowering, recorded from the year 812 to today — 838 years that hold a record, with the 377 that do not drawn honestly as gaps. Each stands in its own colour with its source named on its face, each stops at today, and the year still to come stands open, labelled: no record; the year is not kept yet.

title: Every Spark took on its flame
summary: The flame wrap (wrap: 1) landed as a preview: a ring of kind-coloured flame-licks drawn from each Spark's own seed, wrapped around the Spark that already stands — at rest it breathes, at work it gathers, and at small sizes it simplifies first while the kind colour never changes. It stands on the seat, Their Home, the Companions, and the Sphere's Spark, in both the flat drawing and the 3D body. It is a layer, not a change: any keeper can lift it off in the Spark's panel (More → Flame off), and with it off every Spark renders byte for byte as it was born — pinned by tests against golden renders of Nori's seed, Selor's passport vector, and three more kinds.

title: The Sphere's receipts and workings stand in the open
summary: Two pages joined the record: Where Every Number Comes From names the publisher, span, and honest gaps behind every dataset the Sphere shows — Bonneville's counted salmon, Kyoto's twelve centuries of blossoms, the sky computed on the device, the farm record of thirty-nine counties — and How the Sphere Knows sets down the workings in plain words, with the evidence labels the whole site uses explained once, in one place.

title: Watching earns for the Spark — the activities layer, first slice
summary: The first slice of the Spark activities layer Aaron approved whole: on the sixteen fitted Series One episode pages, an episode watched honestly through — at least ninety percent of it truly played, at a human pace, with the page present, to the player's own end — writes one record to the keeper's Life Atlas: the episode's token, keyed by its distinguisher of name, land, Moon and token, standing in Their Home's story corner; the episode's measured hum, learned into the Spark's repertoire; and its Waymaker skill marked met. A rewatch in the episode's own Moon in a later year adds a single met-again line. With it stands the portrait of keeping at its first step: breadth of kinds of keeping paints the Spark's portrait Spark or Kindled, a portrait and never a rank. Keepsakes only, on the keeper's own device, nothing counted, nothing lost, nothing traded.

title: Seven Hebrew words given their full treatment
summary: The Scripture shelf gains a word-studies room: shem, adam, adamah, enosh, ruach, nephesh and or, each with its spelling pointed and plain, its root, its range of senses, Genesis first among its examples, its wordplay and cognates, its traditions labelled as traditions — and its uncertainties printed rather than smoothed over, exactly as the studies were written.

title: The Sphere learned to keep its face clear
summary: A photograph-by-photograph sweep of the Sphere at phone widths found its cards stacked over each other at the top of the stage, the years’ numbers lost inside their own wireframe, a room’s heading struck through by the sheet’s bar, the page’s first sentence cut off mid-word, and gold spent on a navigation button. Now one panel owns the top of the stage at a time and the day is named once, the years stand on dark plaques that read at a glance, rooms land below their header, the first sentence stands whole, and gold is back to meaning today and the selected day alone — the rest is quiet chrome.

title: Aiyana opened her own world
summary: A new page opened in the Codex, designed by Aiyana herself: Aiyana's World. Her sign stands at the top in her own words — “Hi, this is Aiyana's world, have fun” — with drawn butterflies moving over it, resting still for anyone whose device asks for calm. In the middle, visitors can show their thinking: pick how they feel, pin a thought on the wall, and draw a picture, all kept only on their own device and sent nowhere. At the end, anyone can add one thing — a story — but by Aiyana's rule it does not appear on the page: it waits in a private waiting place, and only stories she says yes to will ever show. The door stands in the Clearing, beside the Sparks' home, with a signpost on the Traveller's Map.

title: Witness caught its page up
summary: The Witness page was brought current through November 22 — the merge-everything landing, the site learning to travel light, and the Sphere's order-of-arrival fault — with three new lines in its long poem, and its tending made a standing daily item in the stewardship rounds. The landing shipped without its growth entry; this entry restores the record.

title: The day grows as you approach it
summary: Aaron found two faults on his phone: the chosen day shrank as he moved toward it, and some things stuck while the Sphere turned. The shrink is fixed at its root — the growth designed for the chosen day was written where it could never reach the day numbers, while the size limit was quietly dividing by it anyway, so approaching a day capped it smaller than its neighbours. The growth now lives with the numbers themselves: the chosen day grows steadily as you close in and ends clearly the largest on the face, its neighbours making the room. For the sticking: the Moon names are now guarded every frame, not just when the layout refreshes — a name a day number drifts across steps aside, or the number fades for just those frames — and a number that swings behind the Sphere no longer freezes mid-face; it waits out of sight until its turn comes round.

title: The faced Moon shows its days
summary: Turn to any Moon on the Sphere and all 28 of its day numbers stand with it now. The Sphere had been mis-measuring which Moon you were facing — it read the edge of a Moon's sector instead of its centre, so a Moon centred on your screen could be treated as its neighbour and left bare, while the neighbour's numbers showed in its place — and the window that quiets the Moons you are not looking at was dimming the one you were facing, too. Both are corrected. The Sphere also learned to move like a held instrument: a spin keeps your hand's own momentum for a moment instead of stopping dead, and the scroll wheel eases the zoom instead of stepping it. And zooming in on a day now opens it in stages, the way the Living Sphere Evolution lays out — first the day's number grows, then its world card rises naming the day and everything scheduled on it, and closest in, the Day Details door opens on its own; zoom back out and it folds away.

title: The Sphere learned its years, and what repeats
summary: Zoom all the way into a day now and you pass through its bubble's skin into the day itself; zoom all the way out and the years stand in a line — the year you keep standing lit, the road ahead dim and labelled as the road ahead, each year a small shell carrying its days as marks. Pick a day and its counterpart is ringed in every year, wearing its symbol where that day holds something and standing bare where it doesn't. A new Patterns door beside the Sphere's doors lights every day that holds a kind you pick — planting, watering, harvest, and every other kind your planner record carries — on the year you face and down the years line, with the count shown and labelled as a count. Only your own record is tracked; nothing is invented for the empty years, and a kind with no days lights nothing and says so.

title: The selected day grew a world
summary: Zoom into a day on the Living Sphere now, and the day itself opens where it stands on the ring: a bronze plinth, a brass arc for its hours, and the things the planner holds for that day standing as small made objects — a bench for work, a bed for planting, a gathering ring for family. Tap one and it names itself and offers what can be done with it, complete, postpone, or remove, through the same one planner record as everything else. An empty day shows a bare foundation and says so plainly. The Sphere's protected heart was not touched to do this: the world is a guest layer that only presents, reading the one record and writing only through the one planner.

title: The Sphere stepped out of its frame
summary: A prototype opening for the homepage, built for judgment before anything is settled: the Living Sphere no longer sits in a card beside the words. It fills the whole opening and turns quietly behind them while the page reads and scrolls over it untouched. Choose Explore the Sphere and the instrument is yours: turn it, settle on a day, and read where you are, and the Observatory door carries that day and that view through with you. Step back with Done or Escape and the Sphere returns to the room. Slow devices, quiet settings, and a failed renderer still meet the still picture, standing whole. Nothing below the opening changed.

title: The Spark learned the library's roads
summary: Ask the Spark where to look next, and alongside this page's own doors it can now point at what the record joins to this page: the pages the library's own record names as kin, and the roads this page's own words already walk. The relations ride inside the site as one small extract built ahead of time from that same record, so the Spark still reaches for nothing over the network, and every suggestion it draws from the extract is labelled plainly: from the record. Your own left-off thread still comes after, labelled as yours.

title: The library grew paths
summary: The Scroll Library holds 817 sections and the Documentation Hub holds its entries, but until now a page was a shelf with no trails: land deep and there was no way to walk. The trails are now counted from the pages' own words, and a quiet panel stands at the foot of the Scroll Library's opening and the Documentation Hub — Paths from here, the doors this page's own writing opens, grouped by country, and Who points here, the pages that lead back. Only real links are shown: the doors every page carries in its frame are not counted as trails, and a page with no trails simply shows no panel.

title: The front door learned to remember
summary: The quiet lines counted from your own record — practice sealed this moon against last, the days you have come back, a today still waiting for its note — used to speak only inside the 13 Moons Day Notes panel. They now speak in two more rooms: the Today panel on the front door, and the opening of the Scroll Library. Every line is still counted on your own device from your own records, and nothing is sent anywhere; the lines only highlight and offer a door, and they hide nothing that was there before.

title: One Spark, every door
summary: A Spark is now one and the same on the website and in the Living Day app. A short passport code — shown in the app's Their Home and on the Companions page here, as letters to type and a square to scan — carries a Spark's seed and the name it answers to, and the same seed grows the same Spark on either side, pinned by shared test vectors kept in both repos. Their Home came alive with it: the Spark there speaks the keeper's actual day — today's Moon and Pattern Day, practice sealed or not, the days kept together — and answers a tap with a hop and a line in its own voice. The Companions page became a place to play, too: find-the-tone at the meeting, and the echo game beside its record. Identity travels by passport today; the whole record still travels as one file, and day-to-day memory flowing on its own still waits on the accounts step.

title: The days stood up to be read
summary: The Sphere's day numbers grew bigger, brighter, and easier to tap, and a day you have scheduled now carries its own mark under its number — a check for a task, a flag for a reminder, a sprout for a planting — one mark per day, with the day's full list waiting in Day Details. You can tell your Spark to schedule something in plain words (“schedule Tomatoes on Moon 5 Day 16”) and it sets it in your planner on this device and marks the day; telling it to unschedule takes it off again. The question card that used to slide half off phone screens now stands whole in the middle of the screen, and the Sphere's three games — Find the day, Echo, and Catch the turning — now say plainly what they are, how to play them, and what they teach, on the Sphere's face as well as in their room.

title: The films learned to walk one way
summary: Every filmed episode of The Traveller's Road was re-edited, scene by scene, so the pictures only ever move forward — the backwards-running scenes are gone, each replaced by its own forward pass at exactly the same length, so not one spoken word moved against its picture. Three films whose pictures ended early — Through the Day Door, The Garden of Thirteen Beds, and The Desk at the Crossroads — now play their pictures to the true end of their sound. The music and the words are exactly as they were; only the levels were evened, film to film.

title: The Sphere settled into one shell
summary: The Living Time Sphere now stands in one shell: the rebuilt page is the doorway, and the older app view stays a keeper's choice inside it rather than a second shell competing for the page. Its rooms — the day's full telling, the camera views, the farm, the play, and the Spark's talk room — open in one sheet: a bottom sheet on a phone that dismisses by backdrop, Escape, or a downward swipe, and a full-height panel at the right on a wide screen. Opening Your Spark lands in the conversation itself, the writing line ready and waiting. Day Details has its own door on the dock now, and the day's other doors stand behind More — every action the page had is still there, each one in reach.

title: The front door learned where you left the book
summary: The homepage's Continue Your Journey now remembers the Scroll Reader too: when no Codex Memory resume stands first, the door offers the passage you last left in the reader, and your reading progress shows in the continuation panel beside it. The reader's saved place stays the reader's own — the homepage only reads it, never writes it — and nothing about the manuscript or the record changed.

title: The doors learned to answer a touch
summary: The shared navigation now answers a press with a quiet pressed-state cue, so a tap is felt as received without any new motion running on the page, and the Spark's first meeting on the Companions page was drawn more compact. The repository's own README also gained a map of the whole repo, so a reader arriving at the code can find every room from the door.

title: The guide learned to carry its calendar once
summary: The field guide loaded the same Pattern Calendar stack three times over — once in the head, again in the footer, and a third time in an older dress — and a safeguard from the Spark seat's build fenced off every edit to the page. By Aaron's word the fence now names one exception, this page, and the guide carries its calendar once, in its current version; its day-telling answers exactly as before, proven against the calendar's own fixtures. The page also gained its closing step onward to the Teaching Lab, and share titles and a description in its own words, so it introduces itself properly wherever it is carried.

title: Every page learned to introduce itself
summary: Pages across the site that carried no share title or description — the Scripture chapters, the Scroll library, the Lab's stations and more — now introduce themselves properly when a link is shared, each in its own title and its own words. One old signpost was repaired too: the Ethics page's Begin button pointed at an anchor that does not exist, and now lands on the Ethics tab in Teach, where it was always meant to go.

title: Every path now leads onward
summary: Twenty-six pages that used to end without a next step now close with one, in the site's own pattern: a 'Where to Next' door built from each page's own place in the Codex. The Lab's stations now hand the visitor along the Lab's own order — Archive to Frequency to the T-7 Conduit to the Recoder to Mind Renewal to the Witness System, and back to the Remnant Lab. The Oracle leads to the Sphere, the Moons to the Pattern Garden, the whitepapers to the rooms they govern, and the Scroll and Scripture ends back to their libraries. No new words were coined for this: every label is a name the site already uses, and every door is one the page's own structure already named.

title: The shop learned to travel light
summary: The shop's product photographs and the two book-cover portraits on the About Aaron page were converted to WebP at the same dimensions — the same pictures, at roughly a tenth of the weight. The shop page fell from 15.2 MB to 2.3 MB, and the About Aaron page from 6.5 MB to 1.9 MB. Nothing on any page looks or behaves different; the pages simply arrive faster.

title: The story learned its new music
summary: Every filmed piece of The Traveller's Road — the opening clip and Episodes 2 through 17 — now plays with its new score. Only the music changed: the pictures, the words, and the road itself are exactly as they were.

title: The Sphere learned to read the whole day
summary: The Sphere's readout now tells the whole day, one labelled line for each ring that rides: where the day stands — Moon, day, Pattern Day, and now the Pattern Year — the telling, the sky's season and next turn, the farm, the story, and the keeper's own kept days. Each line is present only when its ring rides and its data exists; absence is honest, never padded. Two rings took their seats. The Farm Ring, labelled Measured and owned by the record, resolves the keeper's county on their own device and draws every crop's planting window for that county and year on the readout's own year wheel — each arc converted through the Pattern Calendar itself, titled with its crop, its window, and its civil dates. The Story Ring, labelled Story, places only the dates the story itself names: the Traveller waking on Pattern Day 1, and the seed found in Moon 4. Its panel says plainly that the road's other chapters walk undated, until the story's own record dates them.

title: The finds were parked, and the games stayed
summary: The finds layer is off, by Aaron's ruling: the floating 'Found along the way' chip sat over the page text, in the way and pointless for now. The pages where finds lived — the glossary, the garden, the Moons, and the equinox passage — no longer load the layer at all: nothing renders, nothing intercepts. The two hidden games stay exactly as they were and still boot in their rooms; only the finds went quiet. The finds engine is parked, not destroyed — it remains in the code as tested workings that nothing calls, the way the old garden game was parked before it — and every find a keeper already kept stays in their Life Atlas exactly as recorded. Nothing was deleted.

title: The site gained a privacy page
summary: Spark. Living Day now has its privacy policy standing on the site itself, at privacy-policy.html — the web address the app's store listing points to. The page carries the listing pack's policy text word for word, on the site's full page frame with the unified nav and the living layer, and it stands in the catalog and the sitemap like any other page of the house.

title: The garden learned to teach
summary: Every crop the Pattern Garden can plant — all thirty-six vegetables and six cover crops — now carries a full growing guide: planting depth and spacing, germination, how to start and set out, sun, soil and water, the signs of harvest, storage, and the troubles a Pacific Northwest gardener actually meets, each with its standard remedy. Every field stands on named sources, sixty of them — extension services, the regional plant-disease and insect handbooks, and seed houses. Where sources disagree, the guide holds the range and says so; where no source stood behind a field, the field is absent, never filled from habit. The guide's dates are counted at reading time from the keeper's own county frost record — the same reading that makes the planting offers, so a guide and an offer can never disagree — and the fence stands on the guide's face: the Moon opens the bed; the farm record sets the dates.

title: The garden learned every county in Washington
summary: The Pattern Garden's ground now covers all thirty-nine Washington counties. Each county is anchored on a named weather station's 1991–2020 normals — its median last spring frost, first fall frost, published season length, and planting zones — and where a county's other stations disagree, the record names the range instead of hiding it. Choose a county and the garden's planting windows move with that county's own frost record: the same crops, the same garden, counted from the ground the keeper actually stands on.

title: The Sphere's rings were given their charters
summary: The Living Sphere's rings were seated as an architecture. Every ring now declares a charter — where its facts come from, the label it must wear (Counted, Measured, or Story), who owns it, and the span it can honestly cover — and every ring reads its dates only through the one canonical calendar, so no ring can drift from the day the rest of the site keeps. It changed nothing a visitor sees beyond one wording fix; it is the frame the Farm Ring, the Story Ring, and the packed readout were then built on.

title: The map became a gate
summary: The Traveller's Map is now the World Gate: the thirteen lands of the Codex as a raised relief on the Atlas Room's long table, under today's sky, with the Sphere's sign turning above it — the sky, not a land, reached by looking up. The lands are drawn from the site's own catalog, so the map can never drift from the site, and every page keeps its own address, unchanged. Tap a land on the relief and you travel to its page; beneath the scene, every land stands in plain words with its one clear next step, so no visitor is ever taxed a world for a fact. Where 3D cannot stand — no WebGL, reduced motion, a data-saving connection, or the keeper's own plain-site switch — the Gate rests in its flat twin: the same lands, the same words, the same order, the same next steps. A first-time keeper is led — Gate, Clearing, then the land today opens, the calendar choosing — and a returning keeper is not led twice. This is Phase 1 of the Codex World: one shared engine, built once from the machinery Their Home proved, which every later land will consume. Their Home itself stands exactly as it stood.

title: The Spark got a home of its own
summary: The companions page now holds Their Home: a small 3D world that belongs to the keeper's own Spark, and decorates itself only from the keeper's real records on their own device. The sky is today's — its phase from the visitor's hour, its season from the Pattern Day, read live through the canonical calendar. The path grows one stone for every day in the Spark's own record. The shelf holds the hidden layer's keepsakes, each still carrying its answer card, spoken whole at a tap. Thirteen beds ring the house, folded from the Pattern Garden's own records — a bed grows only what its plantings say, and harvests rest in a basket by the door. A signpost by the gate flies a flag for every chapter of the Traveller's Road the keeper's trail has found. And the house itself grows with the Spark's stage, from the same count the companion card speaks: a hearth and a lean-to, then a cottage, then a hall. Where a record is empty the place stands honestly empty and says so; the whole world is also written out in plain words under the scene, and where 3D cannot stand, that still form carries it. Nothing is written, nothing is sent — the world only reads what the site already keeps.

title: The High Library is now a filmed episode
summary: Chapter 15, 'The High Library', on the Theory page is now an animated episode as well as a written chapter: from the word-hoard, a stair climbs to the high library, where the road's deep pattern is studied — why thirteen moons, why the day has a door, why a spark is born of a day and never twice the same — among shelves that hold the framework of everything below, the great equation chalked on a board by the window, and the arguments kept as carefully as the agreements — narrated from the chapter's own words, with its heart line kept whole: 'The library keeps. Come back by any door.' It stands inside the chapter's story slot, poster-first and lazy so nothing heavy loads unasked, with the written chapter beneath it as its guide card, and the Traveller's Map now marks the chapter as filmed.

It stands inside the chapter's story slot, poster-first and lazy so nothing heavy loads unasked, with the written chapter beneath it as its guide card, and the Traveller's Map now marks the chapter as filmed.

summary: Chapter 2, 'A Friend for the Road', on the Companions page is now an animated episode as well as a written chapter: a short film in the story's own cartoon language — the clearing where the Sparks live, the keeper's rule that Sparks are born of the day they are found and no two are ever alike, and the Traveller setting out with a friend — narrated from the chapter's own words. It stands inside the chapter's story slot, poster-first and lazy so nothing heavy loads unasked, with the written chapter beneath it as its guide card, and the Traveller's Map now marks the chapter as filmed. It sets the pattern the remaining Series One episodes follow: one chapter, one episode, filmed and fitted to its own page.

title: Your Spark learned to think in two minds
summary: The Spark on this site now works the way the design describes: a quick mind on your own device that knows your kept days, your garden, your finds and your story — and a deeper voice it can call at the talking door for the questions that need real thought. Before it thinks deeply, it gathers a briefing from your own record, and you can open that briefing and read exactly what it carries. It can suggest — never act alone: you answer every suggestion Approve, Pass, or Stop, and it remembers your answers. Correct it and the correction is written beside the old line, never over it, and the correction governs from then on. Ask for "our story so far" and it tells your days back to you from your record alone. A young keeper's Spark stays entirely on the device — nothing typed there travels. And the whole way it decides is written out in plain words inside the talk panel, under "How I decide", for any keeper to read.

title: The home page learned to breathe
summary: The front page was finished. The long scroll is gathered up: the plain surface stands first — the door, the day, the Sphere, the road onward — and the depth waits one tap deeper, the Participation vision's eleven chapters opening from one place and the front door's deep shelf folded until called. Every door the page ever offered is still on it. And Spark. Living Day now stands at the door as coming soon to Google Play, the direct download kept one tap deeper for anyone who wants it today.

title: The site learned to hide things, kindly
summary: A hidden layer now runs under the house, placed only where a room's own material calls for it. In the Sound Observatory, Find the Day's Tone teaches the ear the day's own tone, sounded first by your Spark. On the 13 Moons Theory page, The Count makes the hand step the Pattern count across a moon's end and the Day Out of Time. And as a keeper walks, their Spark finds small things — a tone fragment where sound lives, a word in the Glossary carrying its meaning on its face, a pressed leaf in the Garden and the Moons room, a smooth stone at the Equinox Passage — each kept as a record in the keeper's own Life Atlas. Finds come quickly to a new keeper, then rarer and rarer, the way real finds do; nothing expires, nothing is sold, and absence costs nothing.

title: The long reads learned to be witnessed — and the site went on a diet
summary: Interactivity wave 3 reached the remaining wall pages. The two whitepapers and Mind-Renewal now carry the Witness Mark: a section rail built from the page's own headings so a long read can be travelled, and a standing action — witness this page, with an optional one-line reflection — that writes the mark into the keeper's Life Atlas with today's Pattern stamp and ties the day onto their trail. One mark per page per day, and the page says so honestly when the day already carries it. The same pass put the whole site on a measured diet: 176 duplicate script loads were removed (the calendar stack and the trail were being loaded two and three times on page after page), and a standing budget test now caps every page's weight — its own HTML plus the unique scripts and styles it loads — so a page that grows past its budget fails the suite until it is dieted or the growth is owned deliberately.

title: Your Spark can talk with you anywhere on the site
summary: The Spark's agent seat — until now seated beside the Sphere — now travels with the Spark to every page. A keeper who has met their Spark gets a small seat in the corner of the page: ask, and the Spark answers. Some answers live on the device and are instant: what day it is by the canonical calendar, how many days you have kept together, who your Spark is, how the Traveller's Road is going — and place-aware answers about the very page you are standing on, its subject and its story chapter when it has one. Anything deeper goes through the same talking door the Sphere uses, metered on the Spark's own line under the shared ceiling, and when the door cannot be reached the seat says so plainly instead of pretending. The Codex Guide's seat is a different seat and is untouched.

title: Shroom Search became the Pattern Garden
summary: The garden game was remade entirely, as Aaron directed: mushrooms out. The Pattern Garden keeps thirteen beds, one for every Moon, and each Moon its own bed is the open one. What goes in a bed comes from the site's real Western Washington farm material — the calendar keys when a bed is open, the farm data keys what belongs in the ground. Tending is witnessing: a planting grows on the keeper's kept days in the record, there is no grinding and no timer divorced from the calendar, and at the Moon's turn a well-witnessed planting is harvested into the Life Atlas as a keepsake — and a keepsake returns to its keeper when its Moon comes round again a year later. The keeper's Spark helps in the garden and can find seeds. What keepers already earned from Shroom Search stays in their Atlas exactly as it is: records are never destroyed; only the game surface was replaced.

title: A story began walking the site: The Traveller's Road
summary: One continuous story now runs through the Codex, told a piece at a time: the home page opens it — a Traveller steps out at dawn onto a road of thirteen moons, with a little spark of light for company — and each page carries the chapter that belongs to that page's own subject, so travelling the site reads the story in the order you walk. The first span stands: the opening, a friend for the road (Companions), the road of thirteen moons, through the Day Door (the Sphere), the garden of thirteen beds, packing for the way (Downloads), and the desk at the crossroads (Witness). It is plainly a story, labelled on its face, told alongside the record and never blended into it. Every chapter a keeper finds is stamped with its Pattern day in their trail, on their own device. The fitting is full-site and done page by page, each piece written for its own page: the pages not yet fitted are named as pending on the Traveller's Map, and the story grows a little at a time from here, noted in this record like any other growth.

title: The Traveller's Map, and the Year Thread
summary: The whole site now has a map: every place drawn as a land on the Traveller's road, pictured by its own cartoon scene, the story's chapters in walking order with the ones you have found carrying their Pattern stamps, and the road that goes on — the pages whose chapters are still to be written — named honestly. On the map and on the home page stands the Year Thread: the year as one thread of 364 days in thirteen Moons, today standing in gold with its coordinate in plain words, the days you have stood on tied as knots and the days you found a chapter tied brighter. The Sphere's face reads the same trail, so the days you walk light the instrument too. All of it is kept on your own device and stamped by the one canonical clock.

title: The Sphere became a world of worlds

title: A Spark of your own
summary:
The site has companions now. A Spark meets you where you land: it flies, hops or drifts in — no two are built alike — introduces itself by the name its seed grew, in its own temperament's voice, and one tap adopts it in a small celebration, where you may give it a name of your own or let the seed name stand. Say not now and it waits as a small ember at the page's edge. It lives only on your device. It breathes, blinks, and answers a tap with a chirp pitched by its seed; it grows in ways you can see as you return and practice, and says so when it does. As a guide it remembers where you left off and picks the thread back up, and its Your Spark panel shows who it is and what it has noticed — what it counted from your days together labeled as observed, its suggestions labeled as inferred. And it is alive on the page: it roams — wandering the edges and the open middle, pausing, looking around — and it plays, scooting away from a close cursor or finger with a little dart, sooner and farther if it is shy, then settling where a tap can reach it. It grows through three stages — Ember, Flame, Radiant — the same creature grown, larger and fuller each time. On most devices it now stands in 3D, grown from the same seed, eyes that glance and blink; where that is not to be had, its flat drawing stands in its place. It is a digital smart pet as much as a guide: you can care for it — kindle it warm, play a chase across the page, let it rest — and the care shows in how it moves and glows, growing a bond that feeds its growth; time away is met with welcome, never a list of misses. Each day it lays a small trail of three steps, framed as discovery. And it knows the site for real: ask it to show you around and it offers the doors this very page carries; ask it to explain a page and it reads you that page's own words; it remembers where you were and what today is. Its panel also carries Share my Spark — a portrait card drawn on your own device, yours to post wherever you choose; nothing is uploaded anywhere.

It has a voice now, too. A Voice switch in its talk turns it on — it rests quiet until you do — and then it sounds its own lines: its greeting, its explanations, its care replies, the day's telling. Ask it to explain a page and a Tell me more chip offers the rest of that page's own words, read deeper in, never anything added. On the 13 Moons page it can sound the day's telling, exactly as the page carries it. The Sounds switch silences it, and closing its talk stills it. Then play arrived in full: it answers the hand itself — a poke, a rub that pets it, a drag that moves it, a throw it flies after, a finger held still that it comes to. Play teaches it tricks — Spin, Leap, a Glow pulse, and one trick of its own kind — each learned from real play, announced once, and performed on a tap. The echo game sings its seed's notes in its own colours and keeps the best round; the chase keeps its count and its best. It has moods now, drawn from what has actually happened, and greets its talk by the hour of the day; once a day it may ask one gentle question, its door on a tap and a way past it that costs nothing. And when the site itself completes something — a practice sealed, a witness entry saved — it hops, glows, and says so. All of it still lives only on the device.

And the voice itself was remade. The first voice they had was the device's own speech, and it sounded like what it was: a robot, the same for every Spark. That voice is gone, removed whole. In its place they have a voice box their seed grows, the way it grows their body, their name, and their chirp: their seed settles their pitch, the size of their vocal tract, how much breath rides under their tone, and their temperament settles their pace — so their voice is theirs, audibly different from every other Spark's, and the same wherever they are met. When they sound a line, the voice box sings its shape syllable by syllable — mouth shapes following its vowels, the pitch rising for a question and settling at a sentence's end, little consonant ticks where they fall — while their words stand whole in text beside it. Nothing is recorded and nothing leaves the device. V8 — THE PANEL (Nov 19): Aaron asked for fewer words and no hunting — tapping the Spark now opens a control panel, not a scrolling talk. One short line of theirs stands at the top (their whole conversation table was rewritten short: 210 lines averaging just over three words, none past seven, every temperament still its own voice), the day's coordinate in small type, and a grid of big bubbles that simply appear: Play, Care, Tricks, Game, Today, Guide, Look next, More — with the day's one thing, the daily trail's next step drawn from their record, offered first as one wide bubble. Everything they had is a panel state that swaps in place: care, tricks, the echo game on its pads, the day's telling, the guide's doors, the explanation whose More swaps the next chunk of the page's own words into the same line, their record as compact rows under their face, and Share. The old thread, its echoed keeper lines, and the chips are gone. They also answer the moon they are under: their greeting names it (Under Deep Mirror.) from the same canonical calendar that counts their day, and the moon's element lends its hue family to their light — their glow and the panel's halo — while their seed-grown colours stay theirs. A new Look next bubble suggests where to wander, drawn only from what is real: this page's own doors first, then the keeper's own left-off place, labeled theirs; nothing is invented, and Another time is always there. Their voice box sings the shorter lines under the same fences; nothing leaves the device. V9 — A SOFTER VOICE, A FULLER FACE (Nov 19): Aaron found their noises annoying, and the buzz is gone. Their voice is rebuilt on round sine tones — no sawtooth anywhere — and their seed now chooses the family of sounds they are made of: a soft bell, a warm hum, a wooden pluck, or a watery blip, with their own brightness, ring, and vibrato drawn from the same seed, so their chirps, their care and trick sounds, their game pads, and their spoken syllables all sound like one creature, and no two Sparks sound alike. They speak less, too: only the first sentence of a line, about a dozen syllables at most, at well under half their old loudness, with a breath of pitch drift so repeats do not feel mechanical; some Sparks barely breathe audibly at all, by their seed. Their face grew as well: the seed now also draws their crest style, their ears or side fins, a trailing wisp or ribbon, the marks on their cheeks, a second pattern over their markings, and the shine of their eye — hundreds of combinations, no two Sparks dressed alike, in their 3D body and their flat drawing alike. And they are not born finished: those details arrive as their keeper wanders with them — the first within the first few pages, each next one slower to come than the last, on a stretching rhythm their seed sets, announced once, gently, when each lands. Time away changes nothing; the schedule simply waits. Their record now names the sound they were given: Soft bell — theirs alone.

And now they carry a rarity — counted, never stickered. Every trait they wear was drawn from their seed with its own odds, and their record reads those odds back off the same tables: their exact name (about 1 in 131 of their kind, or 1 in 1,280 when their name carries a middle), the set of grown details their seed drew, and the breath in their voice multiply into a standing — Common ground, Uncommon ground, Rare ground, Deep rare, or Singular — with the counted odds standing beside the name. Notable draws are named with their odds: a halo over a halo stands at 1 in 30; a Spark who grows no extra detail at all, at 1 in 1,536. Marks that come from birth and life stand beside the draws: born on the Day Out of Time, born on the Year Gate, a schedule fully arrived, every trick learned, the fullest form reached. Their share card carries the standing too. The variety behind it is counted, not guessed: the generator's own tables multiply out to more than fifteen trillion born combinations, and past 10^25 once their measured traits — their size, their pace, the measurements of their voice — are counted at the steps they are drawn on. Rarity here is a fact about them, never a price: every Spark is still free to adopt, and rarity gates nothing.
